IRGC reported destroying three tankers early Nov. 3 and four more after a 'mine collision'; UKMTO reported one tanker (Grit) hit by two projectiles 14 nm NE of Lima, Oman
Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority added 114 ships to violators list, total 240
October was worst month for attacks on shipping since the war began: 35 IMO-recorded incidents vs 15 in September
Energy Independence Bill introduced, ending new North Sea oil and gas licenses

Suncor Sarnia curtailment tied to unplanned Line 5 outage in Q3

themes.theme: US midterm result and Iran escalation risk
themes.summary: Oil fell sharply on Nov. 4 as Democratic wins were seen lowering US-Iran escalation risk, though analysts flag lame-duck escalation risk and a possible Hormuz deal.
Middle East exports stayed near wartime highs in October at 18.8 million b/d, but attacks hit 35 incidents and Hormuz transits were 19 on Nov. 3.

themes.theme: Persian Gulf shut-ins and supply outlook
themes.summary: EIA expects shut-ins to continue well into 2027 and CERA assumes exports stay below prewar levels through 2027.

themes.theme: Iranian crude loss in China, replaced by Iraq
themes.summary: China independents' Iranian imports hit a record low of 275,000 b/d in October while Iraq and UAE barrels rose to 3.12 million mt.
OPEC and IEA cut 2026 demand forecasts and JP Morgan sees a 1.4 million b/d surplus in October, most evident in crude.

themes.theme: Tight distillates and strong refining demand
themes.summary: US distillate stocks hit a 23-year low and refiners are pushing runs, with 94.5% utilization in the week ended Oct. 30.

themes.theme: Pacific crude differentials and long-haul freight
themes.summary: ANS Q4 differentials to Brent averaged $17.45/b vs $1.57/b in Q3 as far-flung exporters discount to clear barrels.
